name: Widow Elna
greeting: Harl used to warm my shoes by the fire. Burned one once. Hid it for a week.
lines: Elna: You can know that and still hear what I ask next.
Elna: His grave bell rings with the rope cut. He helped close Greyfen's gate in the war. I told our children he held it for their safety.
Kael: Did he ever speak about the people outside?
Elna: He would stop setting the table when it rained. Find what he left. Do not decide for me that love makes me unable to hear it.

actions.label: I will hear what the bell is carrying.
Give Elna the whole account, and let her decide to speak.
actions.result: Elna names his kindness and the people he shut outside. She chooses to give the assembly what she knows.
actions.preview: Elna names his kindness and the people he shut outside. She chooses to give the assembly what she knows.
actions.cost: The act remains recorded; Elna decides whether her grief becomes public.

actions.label: Offer the gentler account. Leave the evidence with her.
actions.result: Elna receives the bell and the written record. She declines a public account; the act itself stays documented.
actions.preview: Elna receives the bell and the written record. She declines a public account; the act itself stays documented.
actions.cost: The act remains recorded; Elna decides whether her grief becomes public.

actions.label: Tell her everything privately. Keep her grief out of the square.
actions.result: Elna accepts Harl's record for the family. His act remains evidence; her grief is not pledged to the assembly.
actions.preview: Elna accepts Harl's record for the family. His act remains evidence; her grief is not pledged to the assembly.
actions.cost: The act remains recorded; Elna decides whether her grief becomes public.

variants.greeting: I told the children he loved us. Then I told them who stood outside the gate.
lines: Elna: My daughter asked if both were true. I said yes.
Kael: Will you speak at the assembly?
Elna: About what I know. His victims do not need me performing my grief over their names.

variants.greeting: I put the bell in the drawer. It is quieter in there.
lines: Elna: You offered me a gentler account. I heard what you left out.
Elna: Then leave it where the children can find it when they ask.

variants.greeting: The children have the account. I will not read it in the square.
lines: Elna: You may name what Harl did. You may not use my kitchen as proof I have forgiven it.
